_comment: THE BAZAAR: a compact, lantern-lit souk, always evening. One winding covered lane between sandstone walls: arrive at its east end, it turns north into a little square with a fountain, leaves west, and turns north again to the great arch at the far end (the way home). Stalls line it shoulder to shoulder with someone minding nearly every one; people walk it; lights, bunting and brass lanterns hang overhead; rugs lie on the cobbles; a narrow forgotten alley off the west lane hides the river-drop. Generated by tools/gen_bazaar.py: edit that and re-run, don't hand-tune. 'walls' are segment solids (each with the side its street is on, 'face'); 'roofs' are the buildings beyond them; 'garlands' hang overhead.

props.label: the fountain
props.lore: The fountain in the little square. Its water catches every lantern in the lane, so it's never quite dark here.

props.label: the great arch
props.lore: The great arch at the end of the lane, carved with knots that never quite meet. Beyond it, the way home.

props.label: a man with wet boots
props.lore: His boots are wet, though it hasn't rained here in living memory. He smiles like he knows where the water went, and asks only one thing: have you seen it too?

_secret_comment: This world's one SECRET (docs/home-world-and-secrets-design.md, W-5): no puzzle, a small shiny treasure found only by wandering, at the end of the forgotten alley off the west lane. The server honours a claim only here, within 'radius' of 'position'.

secret.lore: At the very end of the alley, where nobody comes: a single drop of glass, no bigger than a thumbnail. A ripple of light still moves inside it, as if it remembers being water.
secret.found_line: A drop of river-water, kept in glass. Somewhere in the lane, someone once made it hold light instead.

keepsake.label: a drop of river-glass
keepsake.line: The drop of river-glass from the Bazaar. Your companion likes to sit where the light from it falls.

_walkers_comment: Walking traffic: server-simulated like any ambient pal (shared, so everyone sees the same crowd; the walls keep them in the lane), drawn by the client as people from each 'person' appearance.
